summary: Comprehensive backend testing of LLM Council v9 monetization layer (auth, credits, admin, payments, refund). 22/22 pytest tests pass, but ad-hoc exploratory testing uncovered 2 real bugs around refund-on-pipeline-failure.

critical.issue: Credits are debited but NOT refunded when the council pipeline effectively fails. run_full_council() in council.py swallows all model errors and returns HTTP 200 with a stub stage3={'model':'error','response':'All models failed...'} instead of raising. The try/except refund path in main.py:_send_message is therefore never triggered. Reproduction: log in, grant credits, POST to /message without OPENROUTER_API_KEY -> status=200, balance decreases by 10, and no 'refund' row is written. This directly violates the v9 spec: 'Refund on pipeline failure ... credits are auto-refunded'.

Every streamed request fails at Stage 2 with: 'stage2_collect_rankings() got an unexpected keyword argument advanced_config'. main.py:623 calls stage2_collect_rankings(..., advanced_config=request.advanced) but the function signature in council.py does not accept advanced_config. Impact: streaming path is completely broken end-to-end (even with an API key). Silver lining: the exception IS caught and credits ARE refunded correctly on this path (verified: balance restored, refund row written with reason 'Remboursement échec pipeline').

passed_tests: POST /api/auth/dev-login creates new user with role=user and credits=0
GET /api/auth/me returns 401 without cookie, 200 with cookie (httpOnly council_session)
POST /api/admin/users/{id}/credits {amount:100} increases balance; GET /me reflects it
Cross-user isolation: GET /api/conversations/{id} returns 404 for non-owner; GET /api/conversations lists only caller's own
POST /api/admin/models with 'foo/does-not-exist-xyz' -> 400 (OpenRouter public catalog validation works)
PUT /api/admin/chairman validates that model is in council_models
PUT /api/admin/settings/request_cost {standard:7} -> subsequent 402 shows required:7 (cache invalidation works)
POST /api/payments/orders {pack_id:'decouverte'} returns real PayPal sandbox order_id; unknown pack -> 404
GET /api/admin/stats returns total_revenue_cad, credits_purchased, credits_consumed, active_users, requests_7d/30d, recent_transactions
Streaming /message/stream refunds credits on pipeline exception (refund row + balance restored) — spec-compliant
User + credits persist across new dev-login sessions (same UUID -> Postgres persistence confirmed)
action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Make run_full_council raise when all models fail (or main.py must inspect returned stage3.model=='error' and trigger refund). Currently non-stream POST /message silently charges users for failed requests.

FIX (HIGH): Add advanced_config kwarg to stage2_collect_rankings (and any other stageN_* helpers) in council.py so that the streaming endpoint doesn't blow up at Stage 2. Also verify stage1_collect_responses / stage3_synthesize_final accept it consistently.
OPTIONAL: In test_refund_on_pipeline_failure the non-stream branch currently accepts the buggy 200 path; once the fix lands, tighten the assertion to require 502 + refund row.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/main.py:492 send_message wraps only run_full_council in try/except; if the coroutine returns a soft-error dict, no refund happens. Consider either (a) raising in council on all-models-failed, or (b) checking metadata/error after the await and refunding.
backend/main.py:623 stage2_collect_rankings signature mismatch — this call has been broken since streaming refactor.

backend/main.py mixes async SQLAlchemy (asyncpg) and sync psycopg2 (storage.py, settings_store.get_setting_sync) against the SAME Postgres. Works, but doubles the connection footprint and complicates transactions across the two layers.
backend/auth.py: JWT_SECRET has no fallback in prod path but a 'dev-secret' fallback is used in SessionMiddleware — fine because SessionMiddleware isn't used for auth cookies, but worth aligning.

backend/payments.py webhook: request.body() is read but only request.json() is used; verify-webhook-signature should ideally use the raw body for signature integrity (currently PayPal only signs the JSON structure, so acceptable, but noting).
backend/db.py credit_user: when a duplicate paypal_order_id is detected, returns None without rolling back — safe because no writes were issued yet.

success_rate.backend: 91% (22/22 automated pass; 2 real bugs found via exploratory testing)

test_credentials: dev-login: somecedric@gmail.com (admin), any TEST_*@example.com (user). DEV_AUTH=1 enabled in backend/.env.
seed_data_creation: Created ~10 TEST_*@example.com users via dev-login; assorted credit_transactions rows (admin_grant/usage/refund). Non-destructive.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_monetization.py (pytest). Two known backend bugs: (1) non-stream /message doesn't refund on pipeline failure because run_full_council returns 200 with stub error instead of raising, (2) streaming stage2_collect_rankings kwarg mismatch breaks Stage 2. Verify both after fix by re-running the pytest suite AND: curl POST /message without OPENROUTER_API_KEY -> should be 502 with credits refunded (not 200). PayPal capture cannot be automated (requires human approval).
rca of the issue: Non-stream refund miss: council.run_full_council catches per-model errors and synthesizes a fallback stage3 rather than propagating; the FastAPI handler's try/except is therefore dead code in the no-API-key scenario. Mitigation: either raise in council when zero models succeed, or have send_message check stage3.get('model')=='error' (or metadata) and call _refund + return 502. Streaming Stage 2 bug: signature drift between main.py:623 and council.stage2_collect_rankings (missing advanced_config parameter).
